editorial_thesis: Useful agentic systems are being defined by durable execution, visible trust economics, and bounded security operations—not by model novelty alone.

topic_groups.title: Long-Horizon Agent Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: The frontier signal is shifting from “which model?” to “which harness can keep useful work moving for days?” The practical seam is resumability, bounded delegation, and measurable workflow improvement—not unattended autonomy as a demo.

sources.title: Third Moment Research: 10,000 agents for 36+ hours
sources.why_selected: Long-horizon work exposes polling waste, context decay, and failure recovery as first-class engineering problems.
sources.usefulness: Pilot a Buildn research job with an outer supervisor, explicit stop conditions, trajectory logs, and a retry budget.

sources.title: Amp: agents across the product lifecycle
sources.why_selected: The useful unit is a product loop with shared context, not a single code-generation task.
sources.usefulness: Turn a client delivery into linked agents: brief → implementation → visual QA → documentation → launch follow-up.

sources.title: Hermes Agent v0.22.1
sources.why_selected: A local agent runtime is becoming an operating surface with state, identities, plugins, and resumption semantics.
sources.usefulness: Use it as a local-first reference for profile isolation, plugin review, and evidence-bearing delegation in client tooling.

sources.title: DevDay 2026: ongoing agents become a platform surface
sources.why_selected: Clients will ask for ongoing responsibility; the answer needs workspace boundaries, not a bigger prompt.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a “project steward” with a visible queue, approval states, and weekly proof-of-work artifacts.

topic_groups.title: Agent Trust + Unit Economics
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Production adoption is now constrained by the cost of distrust: review, correction, token spend, and unmanaged agents. The strongest response is to make evidence and budgets observable before expanding autonomy.

sources.title: G2: the “Distrust Tax”
sources.why_selected: This reframes ROI: cycle-time gains are real only after supervision, exception handling, and operating cost are counted.
sources.usefulness: Add an agent scorecard to Buildn delivery: outcome, review minutes, correction rate, spend, and rollback count.

sources.title: BigQuery token quotas
sources.why_selected: Token budgets become an enforceable control rather than a dashboard after the bill arrives.
sources.usefulness: Mirror the pattern in client agent gateways: per-project, per-user, and per-workflow budgets with fail-closed behavior.

sources.title: AgentKit sunset is a migration signal
sources.why_selected: Platform churn makes portable traces, prompts, tool contracts, and eval datasets more valuable than UI-specific configuration.
sources.usefulness: Keep client agent definitions in versioned code or exportable specs; preserve eval fixtures and approval logic outside vendor consoles.

topic_groups.title: AI-Assisted Cyber Defense Operations
topic_groups.selection_rationale: The actionable security signal is not “AI finds bugs.” It is a bounded operating loop: correlate evidence, replay against real telemetry, propose a change, and keep accountability with a named reviewer.

sources.title: Block: evidence replay + routed models
sources.why_selected: Security automation becomes safer when every proposed change can be tested against historical telemetry before deployment.
sources.usefulness: Offer a client security review artifact that links finding → evidence → proposed patch → replay result → approval.

sources.title: SentinelOne: malware analysis compressed to hours
sources.why_selected: Speed changes the shape of threat intelligence: analysts can compare families and pursue patterns that were previously too expensive.
sources.usefulness: Use the pattern for safe, offline client analysis: enrich a corpus, surface relationships, and keep final architectural decisions human-owned.

sources.title: GTIG: n-days and AI infrastructure are the risk seam
sources.why_selected: Patch volume alone is a poor control; prioritization must combine exposure, exploitability, and business consequence.
sources.usefulness: Add agent gateway and tool-server exposure to client threat models, then route remediation by exploit evidence.

sources.title: Anthropic Cyber Mission
sources.why_selected: OT environments make “find and patch” insufficient; safe deployment and operational continuity are part of the control.
sources.usefulness: Use the OT lesson for any client system where rollback, uptime, or physical consequences matter: stage, simulate, approve.
